title: Louella's gift of neckties and shirts
summary: She gave him neckties costing ten to twenty dollars and encouraged him to dress like everyone else.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So, anyway, an' I go back downstairs now and take me a bath an' I fool around. Maybe I take me a nap. So when I went back downstairs, Louelly heard me go in the room an' she called me up on the phone. She said, "Come over here. I got somethin' to show you...if you ain't too tired."
Say, "Well, I ain't got nothin' to do. It ain't bother me none."

So I went over to her room, an' she had bought me some brand new neckties. She said, "These some mate that I got the other day. I was waitin' on the right time to give 'em to you because you seem like you don't appreciate nobody doin' nothin' for you."

I say, "Oh, no, that I'm not thataway." I said, "It's okay." I said, "I just didn't want you to spend your money on me and didn't know how you was goin' to get it back." I says, "'Cause I can't keep no money no way." I say, "I spend it fast as I git it. Just luck I had that coupla hundred dollars for you to go down there and buy me some handkerchieves an' stuff, in the first place." I said, "You already bought me some neckties." I say, "You ought...I ain't paid you for them yet."
Say, "Well, these are some more that I got...that I got down there the other day. I was just waitin' on the time to give 'em to ya."
"Well," I said, "they're very pretty." So I was curious, so I say, "Well, how much they cost?"
She say, "Oh, I paid about ten...twenty dollars apiece for 'em."

I said, "Wha-a-a-at?" I say, "Who's gonna know how much a necktie cost?" I say, "Just, generally, most o' time, I wear a bow necktie 'cause I wear a tuxedos," I said, "an' that's somethin' different to wear a straight necktie." I say, "I ain't wore one o' them in a long time."
She say, "Well, I bought you some shirts, too, so you can wear it instead o' that tuxedo you wear all the time. This way you wear your clothes like ever'body else do."
But I used to wearin' tuxedos in New York City so that was just a habit of mine. So I said, "Okay, I dress up like anybody else... so they won't know me from anybody else in the joint."
So I set aroun' there and talk with her awhile, an' she said, "Let's go out and have dinner," so I took off.
Say, "Okay, we go out. We go out...have dinner together."
